$comment: Human-maintained source of truth for the generated HANDOVER.md. Edit this file, run `npm run handover`, never edit HANDOVER.md by hand.

project.name: WACRM Website CMS
project.tagline: Desktop-first SaaS Website CMS, built module by module as a front-end prototype over a simulated backend.
project.stack: React 19 + TypeScript (strict) + Vite 7 + vite-plugin-singlefile; plain CSS design system; no runtime dependencies beyond React; nothing fetched from a CDN, so the artifact works offline from file://.
project.audience: A new engineer or an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex) picking this up cold.

rules: One module at a time: the screen, every CTA/dropdown action, and every operation state — nothing ships half-wired.
Every state must be reachable and code-backed: loading, empty, error, viewer/read-only, conflict, permission denied.
The artifact must open by double-click: single HTML file, no build, no server, no node_modules, no network.
Match the approved mock: typography, spacing, alignment, full-screen fit, no empty gaps.
Never present generated copy as verified fact; no invented claims, no fake analytics.
Dropdown panels must never span the screen. Non-goals: raw HTML/CSS/JS, repeaters, page-level SEO, marketplace, staging, co-editing.
Commit and tag every milestone; keep rollback tags; never persist the GitHub token; rebuild the zip on every change.

modules.name: Overview
modules.notes: Dashboard grid, 6 KPI drawers, funnel, acquisition, site health, publishing rail, release wizard, rollback.

modules.name: Sites & Domains
modules.notes: Define.ai-style two-pane registry, create wizard, DNS/SSL verification, archive/restore, domain checks.

modules.name: Pages & Routes
modules.notes: Registry + tree + inspector, 8 modals, slug/route guards, deep links, trash with restore window.

modules.name: Visual Builder
modules.notes: 3-panel editor, 19 blocks / 23 sections / 5 templates, drag with refusal reasons, token-bounded style, autosave 2 s + CAS, revisions with block diff + restore, AI copy stream, publish handoff into M1.

modules.name: Block library expansion + CRM integration
modules.notes: Industry block-library comparison and the WACRM CRM integration plan (forms, WhatsApp CTA, lead capture, scheduling). Awaiting the user's approval and the clean CRM repo copy.

decisions.decision: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite single-file build; vanilla JS rejected.
In-document canvas for the builder (not an iframe sandbox).
Advanced inspector visible but locked (4 groups).
19 offered block archetypes, 5 inlined generated photos.
Violet #6D4AFF primary, dark sidebar, light #F4F5F7 canvas.
Backend is not built now; every contract is written into BACKEND-PLAN.md instead.
Prototype states are reachable from the beaker menu (Default / Empty / Error / Publish conflict / Viewer).
Deep links are the QA contract: every screen must restore from its hash on a cold load.

next.headline: PROBE
blockedOn: User is uploading a clean copy of the CRM repo (the current EuroMiles-WACRM checkout is NOT the review target).
Push to GitHub needs a fresh PAT (Contents: write) — local commits and tags are complete.
tasks: Re-clone the clean CRM repo and answer three questions against it: does a form builder exist, what channel/inbox APIs exist, how does a public lead endpoint look.
Swap the desktop/tablet/mobile icons to a single drawn family (done in the current build; verify visually after the approval round).
Extend the block registry from 19 to the approved set, keeping the computed counts and category chips honest.
Add a Forms & Engagement source that reads CRM forms by name instead of a hard-coded form block.
Wire the WhatsApp CTA block to the CRM's click-to-chat resolver (token, prefilled message, fallback), with opt-in consent recorded, unchecked by default.

bootstrap: node --version   # 20+ (built and verified on Node 22/26 types)
sudo apt-get install -y libnspr4 libnss3 libatk1.0-0 libatk-bridge2.0-0 libcups2 libdrm2 libxkbcommon0 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 libxfixes3 libxrandr2 libgbm1 libpango-1.0-0 libcairo2 libasound2t64
environment.notes: The apt batch is only needed on a bare Linux container; Chromium launch failures are system libraries, never app bugs. All QA runs against file:///home/user/wacrm-app/WACRM-CMS.html at 1440x900.

suites.covers: M4 screen, panels, drag, AI, autosave, publish, revisions, 3 widths
M3 registry, tree, inspector, modals, deep links
full-page render, console clean, no overflow

contracts.covers: every screen surface of M1–M3 mapped to an endpoint
builder draft CAS, revisions, library, AI stream, publish handoff
every state per module, its trigger and its contract
the binding builder contract and what shipped

traps: Chrome/Chromium will not launch without the apt batch in environment.bootstrap — that is the container, not the app.
A hash-only goto does not reload; deep-link assertions must goto() then reload().
The store rewrites #/<screen> from its own filters after child effects; a screen owning query params must re-assert them on a short timer (builder uses 220 ms).
The builder's global key handler re-registers dialog listeners mid-dispatch — it must stand down while an overlay owns Escape.
QA counts that depend on a library tab are only valid after switching to that tab (#wb-tab-blocks).
Screenshots are WebP only; the workspace is capped at 128 MB and pruned dependency folders do not persist.
The zip must be built with: zip -rq wacrm-app.zip wacrm-app -x 'wacrm-app/node_modules/*' 'wacrm-app/dist/*' 'wacrm-app/.git/*'.
git commit fails with 'Author identity unknown' until a repo-local user.name/user.email is set.
The sandbox drops .git/config between turns, so the origin URL has to be re-added before a push.

firstTenMinutes: Read HANDOVER.md (this file), then MODULE-4-REVIEW.md §J and STATE-COVERAGE.md.
Run npm run qa and confirm the tallies match the table below.
Read handover.config.json — that is where intent, decisions and next steps live.
definitionOfDone: The screen works for every CTA and dropdown, in every state listed in STATE-COVERAGE.md.
tsc --noEmit is clean and the suite for the module is green; no earlier suite regressed.
BACKEND-PLAN.md carries a contract row for every new control.
The commit is tagged module-N-complete, HANDOVER.md is regenerated, and the zip is rebuilt.
